contentBlocks.text: In Grade 3 you compared fractions with the same denominator. Today: compare fractions with DIFFERENT denominators!

To compare 2/3 and 3/4, first find a common denominator by making equivalent fractions: 2/3 becomes 8/12 (×4/4), and 3/4 becomes 9/12 (×3/3). Now that both have the same denominator, you can compare directly: 8/12 is less than 9/12, so 2/3 is less than 3/4. Compare 1/2 and 2/5 by first converting both to a common denominator of 10.
You just compared fractions with different denominators, a real step up from Grade 3! Tomorrow we'll learn a quicker comparison trick using benchmark fractions.

objectives: Find a common denominator to compare two fractions with different denominators
Apply this method to compare 1/2 and 2/5
teacherGuide.facilitationScript:
1. Review this week's equivalent-fractions and simplifying work.
2. Model the 2/3 vs. 3/4 comparison using common denominators.
3. Have the child compare 1/2 and 2/5 using a common denominator of 10.
4. Complete the worksheet.
5. Preview tomorrow's benchmark-fraction shortcut.
differentiationTips: Struggling: work through the conversion to a common denominator step by step, writing out each equivalent fraction explicitly before comparing
Ready for more: ask the child to explain why converting to a common denominator makes the comparison possible
This directly builds on this week's Day 1 equivalent-fractions skill — point out that connection explicitly
teacherGuide.answerKey: 1/2 = 5/10, 2/5 = 4/10. Since 5/10 is greater than 4/10, 1/2 is greater than 2/5.
teacherGuide.standardsRationale: Directly addresses Common Core Grade 4 standard 4.NF.2: comparing two fractions with different numerators and denominators by creating a common denominator, a genuine step up from Grade 3's same-denominator-only comparison.
